title: Nvidia allegedly engineered scarcity by funding AI startups to buy its GPUs
lede: A TechPowerUp write-up, relaying Wall Street Journal reporting, alleges Nvidia funded AI startups so they would buy its GPUs, keeping demand looking strong and absorbing surplus TSMC supply.

points: As quoted in the thread, the report says the aim was to keep demand looking high and move surplus chips from TSMC.
The WSJ account it draws on centres on an August meeting between Huang and his senior finance team.
Per that account, Huang said big cloud customers were moving to other chips and committed wafer and memory purchases were piling up.
Commenters relay that interim CEO Colette Kress had questioned the vendor-financed deals.

points.text: Many note the circular financing was public long ago; what is new is the claim that it cleared excess TSMC supply.
Several point out the story is third-hand, WSJ via Wccftech, and recommend the original, which centres on Kress questioning Huang's dealmaking.
One lays out the mundane case: with chips selling out anyway, funding smaller buyers keeps Nvidia from depending on hyperscalers that build rival silicon.
Commenters split on whether stakes in neoclouds like Nebius are sound strategy or a bet on customers that cannot outlast vertically integrated clouds.
Another argues GPU demand may be real, and the rush to declare the boom over says more about the narrative than the facts.
